title: Wreck and Current
premise: Dominic Zhou, estranged son of the late archaeologist Dr. Mei-Lin Zhou, is drowning in her debts when a flooded river near his mother's last dig site surrenders a bronze chest bearing the seal of Kharvath, a nation erased from every map. The chest contains half of an inheritance ledger that names Dominic's family as custodians of a buried archive — and someone else has the other half, and will kill for it. Hunted by a collector's private army and shadowed by his mother's former rival, Dominic must cross the Serrano Range ahead of the snows to reach the archive before the monsoon seals the passes. In the ice-locked vault he finds not treasure but his mother's recorded confession: she chose the work over him, and chose him as heir anyway. He claims the inheritance on his own terms, buries the archive with an avalanche, and walks out owing no one.
about_author: Cyrus Reyes is a former river guide who spent six seasons leading expeditions through Central Asian borderlands before turning to fiction full-time. His novels are known for their brutal landscapes, contested inheritances, and characters who dig up more than they bargained for.

chapters.title: The River Keeps Its Books
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Working off his mother's debts dredging a flood-swollen river in Kestrel Bend, Dominic hauls up a bronze chest stamped with the seal of Kharvath, a country that officially never existed. The find draws a crowd and a phone call he doesn't make. Beat: reluctant wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Estate of a Stranger
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Sorting his mother's storage unit, he finds photographs of the same seal and a letter naming him 'custodian, second half.' A man named Voss arrives asking polite questions about the chest. Beat: grief weaponized into suspicion.

chapters.title: Half a Ledger
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Inside the chest: half of a vellum ledger mapping an archive beneath the Serrano Range, plus his mother's field notes in cipher. Voss's men ransack his apartment that night; Dominic escapes with the ledger and nothing else. Beat: the past becomes a debt collector.

chapters.title: The Rival at the Doorstep
chapters.summary: Ines Marchetti's POV. His mother's old rival, archaeologist Ines Marchetti, intercepts Dominic at a bus depot, claiming she can read the cipher — and that Voss works for the Halvard Collection, which buys history and buries people. Uneasy alliance forms. Beat: distrust offered as a lifeline.

chapters.title: Cipher of Small Cruelties
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On a night train east, Ines cracks the first cipher layer using memories only she and Mei-Lin shared. Dominic learns his mother documented everything except how to be his parent. Beat: intimacy through translation.

chapters.title: Kharvath, Erased
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. In a border-town archive, they confirm Kharvath was struck from maps after a 1953 purge; its scholars hid their life's work in the range. Voss's team is two days behind them. Beat: history as a crime scene.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Price
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. To cross the frontier river they bribe a smuggler ferryman, Tam, who recognizes the seal — his grandmother fled Kharvath. He joins them, bringing a boat and grudges. Beat: found family, transactional at first.

chapters.title: First Blood on the Water
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Voss's men ambush the ferry at dawn. Tam runs the rapids, losing the boat but gaining the lead. A mercenary drowns holding a photograph of Dominic. Beat: the hunt turns lethal.

chapters.title: Foothills, First Snowline
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. They reach the range foothills as weather reports warn of early snows. Ines reveals Voss once betrayed Mei-Lin on a dig, leaving her to take the fall. Beat: anger reorganizing into resolve.

chapters.title: The Village That Remembers
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A highland village keeps oral songs of the 'buried library.' An elder tests Dominic with questions about his mother; his honest answer — 'she chose the work' — earns passage. Beat: memory as inheritance.

chapters.title: Ledger, Second Reading
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Deciphering further, Dominic realizes the ledger's second half isn't lost — his mother mailed it somewhere before she died. The postal trail leads back toward the coast they just fled. Beat: hope with a hook in it.

chapters.title: Voss Ascending
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss interrogates the drowned mercenary's contacts, closes on the village, and reflects on the Collection's philosophy: provenance belongs to whoever pays. Beat: cold competence, human void.

chapters.title: Burning the Songs
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Voss's men torch the village granary to force cooperation. The elder dies pointing the way up-valley, buying the trio hours. Guilt lands hard on all three. Beat: cost made visible.

chapters.title: The Goat Path
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A three-day climb on a path built for goats and smugglers. Altitude sickness fells Ines; Dominic carries her pack and her doubts about whether Mei-Lin ever trusted anyone. Beat: endurance as devotion.

chapters.title: Cache at the Col
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. At a mountain col they find a supply cache Mei-Lin planted years ago — dated after she stopped writing to Dominic. Inside: food, rope, and the second half of the ledger, addressed to 'my child, if you're reading this.' Beat: love delivered too late to feel like love.

chapters.title: Reading Her Handwriting
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Alone on watch, Dominic reads the completed ledger: coordinates, and a personal note admitting she sent him away to keep the Collection from using him. He doesn't forgive her; he understands her. Beat: grief reframed.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. An early storm pins them in a snow cave for two days. Rations thin. Tam tells the story of his grandmother's escape from Kharvath; Dominic realizes they're all carrying other people's countries. Beat: forced stillness, shared weight.

chapters.title: The Turn Back Offered
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines, frostbitten, urges turning back; the monsoon will close the southern approach regardless. Dominic refuses — the archive is the only thing that's ever been his. Fracture in the alliance. Beat: ambition versus survival.

chapters.title: Descent Into the Dry Valley
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. They descend into a rain-shadow valley where the ledger's landmarks match: a split rock, a dry riverbed, a cairn of black stones. Someone has been here recently — boot prints under fresh scree. Beat: arrival shadowed by pursuit.

chapters.title: The Sealed Door
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Behind the cairn: a Kharvathi door mechanism requiring both halves of the ledger as keys. It opens onto a stair descending into warm dark. Behind them, engines echo up the valley. Beat: threshold terror.

chapters.title: The Archive of a Dead Nation
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The vault: thousands of sealed cylinders — seed stocks, maps, recordings, a civilization's insurance policy against erasure. Not gold. Memory, deliberately preserved. Beat: awe that rewrites what 'treasure' means.

chapters.title: The Recording Booth
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Among the cylinders, one bears Mei-Lin's name. She recorded her confession inside this room. Ines urges destroying it; Dominic insists on listening. Beat: loyalty tested by curiosity.

chapters.title: Mei-Lin Speaks
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. His mother's voice fills the vault: how she found the archive, how the Collection killed her partner, why she erased herself from Dominic's life to draw the hunters away from him. She ends: 'I leave you the choice I never had.' Beat: the emotional core of the book.

chapters.title: Voss at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss enters the vault with six men, offering Dominic a clean ledger — his debts paid, his mother's reputation restored — in exchange for the archive's location index. Beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: The Bargain Refused
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic refuses: some things aren't currency. Voss orders the vault stripped and the witnesses buried. Standoff in the dark among ten thousand voices of the dead. Beat: line drawn in stone.

chapters.title: Collapse Protocol
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam triggers the vault's ancient countermeasure — a designed avalanche channel meant to entomb the archive rather than surrender it. Chaos, gunfire, falling stone. Beat: the dead defend themselves.

chapters.title: Buried Alive
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Separated from Ines and Tam, Dominic is trapped behind a rockfall with Voss, both injured, air thinning. Two enemies share a candle and silence. Beat: hatred worn down to recognition.

chapters.title: What Voss Wants
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Trapped, Voss confesses: he was Mei-Lin's dig partner, the one who survived the betrayal, and the Collection owns him body and debt. He didn't come for glory; he came because there's no other exit for him either. Beat: villain humanized without absolution.

chapters.title: Digging Out Together
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Archaeologist and looter dig side by side toward a fissure of daylight. Voss takes the worst of a secondary collapse clearing Dominic's path. Beat: grudging grace between enemies.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Outside, Ines and Tam, believing Dominic dead, begin the retreat south as monsoon clouds stack on the horizon. Ines grieves in the register of a rival: cataloguing everything Mei-Lin saw in him. Beat: mourning mistaken for certainty.

chapters.title: Reunion in the Rain's Shadow
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Carrying a dying Voss's testimony recorder, Dominic catches the others at the valley mouth as the first monsoon rain hits. Voss dies giving evidence against the Collection. Beat: relief and loss in the same breath.

chapters.title: Running the Monsoon
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The descent becomes a race: swollen rivers, washed-out trails, a race against the season itself. Tam navigates by his grandmother's escape routes, reversed. Beat: landscape as antagonist.

chapters.title: The Flood Crossing
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. At the last river, the bridge is gone. They cross on a rope Tam rigs, and the ledger — the original — goes into the water. Dominic lets it go. The coordinates live in his head now. Beat: release of the object, keeping of the meaning.

chapters.title: Border Light
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. They cross into neutral territory as the passes close behind them, sealed by snow and rain until spring. Whatever happens next cannot be undone or followed. Beat: exhaustion edged with freedom.

chapters.title: Press Conference, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Instead of selling the story, Dominic delivers Voss's recording to an international heritage tribunal, burning the Collection's cover. His debts dissolve in the scandal's wake. Beat: justice chosen over profit.

chapters.title: What Ines Kept
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines admits she photographed pages of the ledger before the river took it — not to sell, but because she couldn't bear a world with no record. She gives the film to Dominic. Trust, finally earned. Beat: rivalry resolved into kinship.

chapters.title: Custodian, Second Half
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Spring. Dominic returns to the valley mouth with a small sanctioned expedition — Ines, Tam, and Kharvathi descendants — to excavate properly, slowly, on the community's terms. Beat: inheritance reclaimed as responsibility.

chapters.title: The Door Opens Again
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The vault stands open where the avalanche fell short of the inner chamber. The cylinders are intact. Dominic records his own message for whoever comes next, choosing words his mother never found. Beat: cycle continued, consciously.

chapters.title: Kestrel Bend, Repaid
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Back at the river where it began, Dominic pays off the last of his mother's debts with money he no longer needs, and dredges up nothing but ordinary mud. Beat: the debt closed, the compass quiet.

chapters.title: Wreck and Current
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, closing. Standing at the water's edge with the repaired compass that points nowhere useful, Dominic understands his inheritance was never the archive — it was the choosing. He walks upstream, into the current, unburdened. Beat: resolution as forward motion.
